q1: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2: SELECT IFNULL(( SELECT M1.NUM FROM MYNUMBERS M1 WHERE (SELECT COUNT(1) FROM MYNUMBERS M2 WHERE M2.NUM = M1.NUM) = 1 ORDER BY NUM DESC LIMIT 1), NULL ) AS NUM

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 finds the maximum number among distinct values in MYNUMBERS (i.e., the maximum unique number). Q2 finds the maximum number that appears exactly once in the table. These two queries can yield different results if there are duplicate values that are not the maximum.
counterexample_dsp: A test case where there are duplicate values for a number less than the maximum number. Q1 will return the maximum number (which is unique), while Q2 will also return the same number since it appears once. However, if the maximum number appears more than once, Q1 would still return it but Q2 would return the next unique maximum.
